title: Verity autonomy policy
description: Schema for .verity/autonomy.yml (verity-autonomy-technical-sketch.md §2). All keys are optional; the effective policy is the file deep-merged over the defaults shown here. HARD INVARIANTS enforced in code, beyond this schema: review.low_risk.protected_paths always includes '.github/**' and '.verity/**'; gates always includes 'golive'; mode 'manual' means the autonomy worker exits 0 immediately with 'autonomy disabled'.

auto_advance.description: Roles allowed to chain without a human gate (supervised+).

gates.description: Pause points that ALWAYS wait for a human. 'golive' is forced in code even if removed here.

trust.description: Reviewer merge authority: 0 none, 1 low-risk auto-merge, 2 full. Raising it via the CLI requires --confirm and records an ADR.

protected_paths.description: '.github/**' and '.verity/**' are forced in code even if removed here.

unknown_cost_behavior.description: What the worker does when a role reports UNKNOWN cost (est_usd null — never $0, ADR-0008). 'gate' pauses at the existing human gate (default until a provider's cost accounting is proven), 'fail' stops the run, 'allow_with_token_limit' proceeds bounded by token ceilings alone. Null never counts against the daily budget breaker.

unverified_ci_behavior.description: ADDITIVE, DEFAULT-ABSENT (stage 19, issue #50). What the worker does when a PR's CI cannot be VERIFIED — GitHub reports no checks at all for it, so 'no CI configured' and 'CI failing' are the same observation. Absent = 'gate': the run pauses at the ci:unverified human gate, because Verity cannot honestly claim the stage is green or that it is red. 'allow_without_merge' lets the stage advance to review instead, for repositories that legitimately have no CI. NEITHER value can merge on unverified CI: merge requires a VERIFIED green reading (trust.checksGreen for the autonomous ladder, review.canMerge for the CLI), which an unchecked PR can never produce.

humans.description: Logins; a bot token matching any of these refuses to start.

commit_usage.description: Worker commits .verity/usage.csv after each run with message 'chore(verity): usage <run-id>' (verity-autonomy-technical-sketch.md §3.4).

agent.description: Which model runtime the autonomy worker drives (stage 9, ADR-0005/0007/0009). Defaults keep every pre-existing policy Claude-backed; codex requires an explicit provider edit. The worker resolves ONE immutable effective config per run from this block. NO unrestricted-access value exists anywhere in this schema (ADR-0007).

provider.description: Headless runtime the worker dispatches roles to.

model.description: Optional model override passed to the provider; null = the provider's default.

sandbox.description: Codex-only sandbox override. May only NARROW the role's .permissions.json projection — read-only over workspace-write is allowed, the reverse is refused (fail closed, ADR-0007). 'danger-full-access' is not representable.

approval.description: Codex-only approval-policy override. May only NARROW the role's projection ('never' permits the least human-mediated escalation).

ignore_user_config.description: Headless runs ignore the user's global provider config by default so it cannot change autonomous behavior (ADR-0007). The role's .permissions.json projection governs each invocation.

acknowledged_enforcement_gaps.description: ADDITIVE, DEFAULT-ABSENT (stage 11, ADR-0011 capability honesty rule). Capabilities whose DENIAL Verity cannot enforce on the selected provider, acknowledged explicitly by the operator. Today the only such capability is 'network': codex exec ignores permission profiles, so a role declaring network:false is REFUSED (exit 30 unenforceable-policy) unless listed here. Listing a capability grants nothing — it records that its denial is unenforced, and every affected run's result carries that admission. Codex-only.

containment_tier.description: ADDITIVE, DEFAULT-ABSENT (stage 14, ADR-0011). Which enforcement tier the worker demands of every codex dispatch. Absent = tier 1: credential stripping plus mandatory post-run invariants, which catch a containment violation AFTER it happened and revert what is safely revertible — adequate for supervised/trust-0. 2 = additionally run each role in a DISPOSABLE SHAPED WORKSPACE (paths the role may not touch are physically absent) with a GATED MERGE-BACK deciding what propagates into the real repository, making the violation impossible to propagate. UNATTENDED codex autonomy (mode: autonomous) is REFUSED below 2 (exit 30 containment-tier-required). Codex-only — claude has no containment tiers.

roles.description: ADDITIVE, DEFAULT-ABSENT (stage 54, ADR-0024). Optional per-role override map: keys are the roles the worker dispatches (build|plan|review), values are PARTIAL agent configs (provider/model plus the codex knobs) validated with the SAME enums as this block. Resolved ONCE at run start and FROZEN by the worker (never re-read mid-run), with containment enforced per role — a per-role codex override still requires tier 2 under mode: autonomous. Overrides may only NARROW a role's sandbox/approval relative to the base. Absent ⇒ byte-identical to a worker-wide agent config (the feature's kill-switch). An unknown role key is a load error (fail closed).

substrate.description: ADDITIVE, DEFAULT-ABSENT (stage 79, ADR-0029). Which delivery substrate the run targets. Resolved ONCE at run start onto the effective policy and frozen for the run (the ADR-0024 agent-block pattern): absent resolves to 'github' — byte-identical engine behavior to every pre-stage-79 policy, and no default is ever written into provisioned files (absence is the kill-switch). An unknown value is a fail-closed load error naming the key and its allowed values — never a silent default. 'local' EXECUTES as of stage 83: the stage-79 refusal is lifted — the local substrate driver landed across stages 80–85 (record store + snapshot acquirer, bare-origin git lifecycle with the engine-performed merge, SHA-pinned gate runner, substrate-aware worker gh sites) and a local run proceeds end-to-end with zero GitHub API calls; the worker's assertSubstrateSupported belt still refuses any value outside the enum — the engine never proceeds half-driven.

gate_runner.description: ADDITIVE, DEFAULT-ABSENT (stage 86, ADR-0030). WHERE the committed gate definition executes — orthogonal to 'substrate' (where truth lives). Values: the literals 'direct' (the stage-82 engine-spawned runner on this machine), 'localhost' (act in Docker on this machine), 'github-actions' (CI check rollups on a pushed branch — the github substrate's native oracle), or 'remote:<name>' (act over SSH on a host named in the gate-runner catalog; <name> is non-empty and catalog-name-safe). Resolved ONCE at policy load onto the effective policy and frozen for the run: absent resolves to the substrate's native runner — 'direct' on substrate 'local', 'github-actions' on substrate 'github' — byte-identical to every pre-stage-86 policy, and no default is ever written into provisioned files (absence is the kill-switch). An unknown value (including 'remote:' with an empty or unsafe name) is a fail-closed load error naming the key and its allowed values — never a silent default. Rejected combinations, refused fail-closed at load: substrate 'local' + gate_runner 'github-actions' (it presumes a pushed GitHub branch the substrate says does not exist); substrate 'github' + any non-'github-actions' runner (not supported in v1 — admitting it later is additive). 'localhost' EXECUTES as of stage 87: the engine renders a gates workflow from the committed .verity/gates.json at the pinned sha and runs it under nektos/act in Docker on this machine, judged by act's exit code only; a machine that cannot serve it (Docker binary/daemon or act absent, act version unparseable) refuses fail-closed at preflight — NO record, the branch stays UNKNOWN, never a silent degradation to 'direct'. 'remote:<name>' EXECUTES as of stage 89: the name resolves against the ~/.verity/gate-runners.md catalog (a typo is a fail-closed CONFIG error naming the catalog path and known entries), the pinned sha is pushed to a Verity-owned runner-side clone over the operator's existing SSH context (BatchMode, prompt-free; auth never read or logged), and the same rendered workflow runs under act in Docker there, judged by act's exit code only — the record carries the catalog NAME only, never host, user, or key paths. An unreachable or unprovisionable runner (SSH down, remote Docker/act absent, runner-side sha mismatch, wall-clock timeout) refuses fail-closed at preflight or before the record — NO record, the branch stays UNKNOWN, and the engine never silently executes on a different runner than configured (no fallback chains in v1).
